Perfect. I am looking forward to it.

Four and seven. They have a lot of energy, but they are good fun.

It is quite cold, yes. There was frost on the cars this morning.
We had the same. I had to scrape the windscreen for the first time this year.
Winter seems to have arrived all at once.

The forecast says so, but only in the evening. The afternoon should stay dry.

Then I would go soon, just to be safe.

That is fair. It is much nicer to watch from indoors.

Spring, I think. I like it when the evenings start to get lighter.

The colours are hard to argue with.

I think so, if the drive is not too long. Mountain air does a lot in a short time.

I am thinking about learning to code, but I do not know where to start.
Many people begin with Python, because it reads quite clearly. Do you have something you would like to build?
I would like to automate some of the spreadsheets I use at work.
That is a very good first goal. Having a real task makes it much easier to keep going.
How long does it take to get anywhere?
I am not sure for everyone, but a few weeks of regular practice is often enough for small, useful scripts.
Is it too late to learn programming at forty?
Not at all. Plenty of people start later than that and do well.
Which language should I learn first?
It depends on what you want to do, but Python is a common first choice.
Why Python in particular?
It is fairly readable and it is used for many things, from small scripts to data work.

That is normal, even for experienced people. What are you stuck on at the moment?
Loops. I understand the examples, but not how to write my own.
That gap is very common. Try changing a working example a little at a time and see what happens.

For most everyday programming, not especially. Clear thinking matters more.
That is a relief. Maths was never my subject.
You will be fine. You can learn the parts you need when you need them.
How much time should I practise each day?
Regular short sessions tend to work better than rare long ones. Half an hour a day is a good start.
I can manage half an hour.
Then you are in a good position. Consistency matters more than the amount.

It felt better than I expected.

I get an error message and I do not understand it.

Something about an unexpected indent on line four.
That usually means the spacing at the start of that line does not match the lines around it. Check for extra spaces.
You were right. There was a stray space.

The terms overlap a lot. Engineer often suggests more attention to design and to working in a team.

In many companies, yes. The actual work can be very similar.
My daughter asked me why the sky is blue, and I realised I did not know.
It is because of how sunlight scatters in the air. Blue light is scattered much more than red light.
So the blue comes from all directions, not only from the sun?
Yes, exactly. That is why the whole sky looks blue during the day.
Why is the sky blue and not violet, if violet scatters even more?
Good question. The sun gives off less violet light, and our eyes are less sensitive to it.
So it is partly about how we see?
Yes. The sky is a mix, and to our eyes that mix looks blue.
Why does the sky turn red at sunset?
At sunset the light passes through much more air. Most of the blue is scattered away before it reaches you.
And the red is what is left?
Exactly. Red and orange light get through more easily.
Is the sky blue on other planets?
Not always. On Mars the daytime sky looks more butterscotch, because of the dust.
I did not know that. What about the sunsets there?
They look bluish near the sun, which is the reverse of ours.
Why is the sky black at night?
Because the sun is no longer lighting the air above you. Without that light there is nothing to scatter.
Is the sea blue because it reflects the sky?
Only partly. Water itself absorbs red light, so deep water looks blue.
So it would be blue even under a grey sky?
Deep, clear water would still look bluish, though duller.
Why are clouds white if the sky is blue?
The droplets in clouds are much larger than air molecules. They scatter all colours about equally.
And all colours together look white?
Yes, that is right.
My son asked why the sky is blue and I said because it is. Was that wrong?
It is not much of an answer, but most parents have given it. Would you like a simple version?
Yes, please. He will certainly ask again.
You could say that sunlight is made of many colours, and the air bounces the blue around the most.
Who worked out why the sky is blue?
The explanation is usually credited to Lord Rayleigh in the nineteenth century. The effect is named after him.
Is that what people call Rayleigh scattering?
Yes, that is the one.
Is the sky blue in space?
No. Above the atmosphere there is no air to scatter the light, so the sky looks black.
Even with the sun shining?
Yes. Astronauts see a bright sun in a black sky.
